quests.instruction: Your pencil point is blunt and makes thick, messy lines. What would help?
quests.hint: Think about what could make the tip thin and pointed again.
quests.explanation: A sharpener shaves the wood and graphite to make a fresh, thin point for neat writing.
quests.funFact: Pencil shavings are just thin curls of wood and graphite.

quests.instruction: You are making a poster title that people should read from across the room. What should you use?
quests.hint: Pick the one that makes bold, bright lines.
quests.explanation: Markers make thick, bright lines that are easy to read from far away. Pencil lines are thin and light.
quests.funFact: Markers have a fiber tip that is kept moist by ink, so keep the cap on.

quests.instruction: You find a word you don't know in a story. Which book can tell you what it means?
quests.hint: It lists words in ABC order with their meanings.
quests.explanation: A dictionary gives meanings of words and often shows how to say them.
quests.funFact: In a dictionary, words are listed in alphabetical order so you can find them fast.

quests.instruction: You want to know if today is Tuesday or Wednesday. What do you check?
quests.hint: It shows days, weeks, and months.
quests.explanation: A calendar shows the date and day, so you can plan ahead.
quests.funFact: A week has seven days, and a year has 52 weeks plus a day or two.

quests.instruction: Your teacher says you have five minutes left to finish. What do you look at to see how long is left?
quests.hint: It tells the hour and the minutes.
quests.explanation: A clock shows the time of day, so you can see how many minutes are left.
quests.funFact: There are 60 minutes in one hour.

quests.instruction: Where can you see which lesson comes after break on a Monday?
quests.hint: It lists lessons by day and time.
quests.explanation: A timetable lists what subject is taught at what time, so you can get ready for each lesson.
quests.funFact: Many schools give each student a copy of the timetable to keep in their bag.

quests.instruction: Where can you hang your coat and keep your bag safe until you need it?
quests.hint: It's a storage space with a door.
quests.explanation: A locker or cubby gives each student a place for their coat and bag, so the classroom stays clear.
quests.funFact: Lockers often have a number so each student knows which one is theirs.

quests.instruction: After snack time, where does a banana peel go?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with waste.
quests.explanation: Food scraps go in the trash can so the classroom stays clean and doesn't attract insects.
quests.funFact: Some schools put fruit peels in a compost bin to make soil for gardens.

quests.instruction: You finished your worksheet. Where do you put it so the teacher can collect it?
quests.hint: It's a tray for finished work, not for your own things.
quests.explanation: A homework tray collects finished work in one place, so nothing gets lost.
quests.funFact: An 'in tray' is a tray where finished papers are placed to be checked.

quests.instruction: What do you need to show to take a book home from the library?
quests.hint: It has your name on it and tells the library who is borrowing.
quests.explanation: A library card tells the librarian who has borrowed which book, so the book can come back.
quests.funFact: Many libraries today scan a barcode on the card and on the book.

quests.instruction: You finished reading your library book. What should you do?
options: Keep it in your desk for the term 🗄️
Keep it at home until you want it again 🏠
quests.hint: Others are waiting to read it too.
quests.explanation: Returning books on time lets the next reader enjoy them, and nothing goes missing.
quests.funFact: A book can be borrowed by many different readers over the years.

quests.instruction: How should you speak while others are reading in the library?
quests.hint: Think about everyone trying to concentrate.
quests.explanation: A soft voice lets everyone read and think in peace. If you need help, whisper to the librarian.
quests.funFact: Many libraries have separate quiet reading areas and group study areas.

quests.instruction: What flat holder do you carry your plate and cup on when you collect your meal?
quests.hint: It is flat, and has a raised edge so things don't slide off.
quests.explanation: A tray lets you carry food and drink with both hands while you walk to your seat.
quests.funFact: Trays often have separate sections for each part of a meal.

quests.instruction: What should you do before you eat your lunch?
quests.hint: Think about what your hands touched during the morning.
quests.explanation: Washing your hands before eating removes germs, so they don't get into your food.
quests.funFact: Soap and water for 20 seconds works well for removing germs.

quests.instruction: The lunch line is long. How should you wait?
quests.correctAnswer: Stand in line and wait your turn 🚶
options: Stand in line and wait your turn 🚶
Slip in beside a friend near the front 👫
Push through the crowd with your tray 🍽️
quests.hint: Others have been waiting too.
quests.explanation: Waiting in line is fair to everyone, and it keeps the cafeteria safe and calm.
quests.funFact: Waiting in line is called queueing in British English.

quests.instruction: Where would you play a ball game that needs lots of open space?
quests.hint: It is outdoors, and it has a lot of grass.
quests.explanation: A school field has plenty of room for running and team games like football or cricket.
quests.funFact: A football pitch is more than 90 meters long.

quests.instruction: Which playground equipment is for climbing up and across?
quests.hint: Your hands and feet grip bars as you go up.
quests.explanation: A climbing frame helps build strong arms and legs, and also helps you learn balance.
quests.funFact: Climbing uses your arms, legs, and core muscles all together.

quests.instruction: Many children want to use the slide. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Wait for your turn at the ladder 🪜
options: Climb up the slide to get ahead of others ⬆️
Wait for your turn at the ladder 🪜
Squeeze past the child on the ladder 🧗
quests.hint: Think about how everyone gets a turn.
quests.explanation: Taking turns keeps the slide safe, since two children on it at once can bump into each other.
quests.funFact: On a slide, sitting and going feet first is safer than head first.

quests.instruction: You want to mix red and yellow to make a new color. What will you mix them on?
quests.hint: It's a flat surface where paint colors are mixed.
quests.explanation: A palette holds small amounts of paint so you can mix new colors before you use them.
quests.funFact: Mixing red and yellow makes orange.

quests.instruction: You've finished painting. Where should you rinse your brush?
quests.hint: Brushes need water, then to be dried.
quests.explanation: Rinsing your brush in the sink stops paint from drying in the bristles and ruining the brush.
quests.funFact: Rinsing a brush right away helps it last for many projects.

quests.instruction: What protects your clothes from paint splashes?
quests.hint: You wear it over the front of your clothes.
quests.explanation: An apron covers your clothes, so paint or glue stays off them.
quests.funFact: Aprons for art are often made from material that wipes clean.

quests.instruction: Which equipment do you swing over your head and jump over?
quests.hint: You hold the handles at both ends.
quests.explanation: Jumping rope is good exercise for your heart and helps with timing and coordination.
quests.funFact: Jumping rope is a favorite exercise of many athletes, including boxers.

quests.instruction: Which bright object is placed on the ground in PE to show a path or boundary?
quests.hint: It stands up like a small hat.
quests.explanation: Cones mark where to start, turn, or stop, so everyone knows the boundaries of the game.
quests.funFact: Cones are often brightly colored so they are easy to see.

quests.instruction: What soft surface do you use for rolling or stretching safely in PE?
quests.hint: It's soft, thick, and sits flat on the floor.
quests.explanation: A mat cushions your body when you roll or stretch, so the floor doesn't hurt.
quests.funFact: Gym mats are filled with foam to absorb bumps.

quests.instruction: Which part of a computer do you move with your hand to point at things on the screen?
quests.hint: Clicking it selects what you point at.
quests.explanation: A mouse moves a pointer on the screen, so you can select things.
quests.funFact: Many mice have a small wheel for scrolling up and down.

quests.instruction: Which part of a computer do you press to type letters and numbers?
quests.hint: It has rows of keys.
quests.explanation: A keyboard lets you type words and numbers, and each key has a letter, number, or symbol.
quests.funFact: Most English keyboards put the letters in a layout called QWERTY.

quests.instruction: Which machine puts your finished work onto paper?
quests.hint: Paper goes in, and a copy of your work comes out.
quests.explanation: A printer turns what's on the screen into a paper copy that you can hold and share.
quests.funFact: A printer adds tiny dots of ink or toner to make words and pictures.

quests.instruction: A green sign shows a person running toward a door. What does it mean?
quests.hint: It points the way out of the building.
quests.explanation: This sign shows the way out in an emergency. Never block an exit door.
quests.funFact: Exit signs are often lit up so they can be seen even in smoke or when the lights go out.

quests.instruction: A picture of a phone has a red line through it. What does it mean?
quests.hint: A red line across a picture usually means 'don't'.
quests.explanation: Signs with a red circle and a line tell you something is not allowed, like using phones.
quests.funFact: Red often means stop or don't, and many countries use the same signs.

quests.instruction: A sign with a white cross on green shows where to find what?
quests.hint: It is the symbol for medical help.
quests.explanation: A first aid sign shows where to find supplies to help someone who has been hurt.
quests.funFact: The green and white cross is used as a first aid symbol in many countries.
